description: The spacing scope of Accessible first: its answers, its usage rules and the semantic tokens it owns. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

answers.question: spacing.roles
answers.why: Large rows matter for touch and zoom.

answers.question: spacing.count
answers.why: One density; no compact mode to fail people.

usage.why: Items in one group sit 16px apart, not the 12px tight gap: generous space between fields stops mis-taps.
Space is easy to see; thin lines are not.
Large rows are easy to read and tap.
Parts sit close enough to read as one item, with room to tell them apart at high zoom.
Space between fields lowers mis-taps for people with tremor.
A clear break shows where one group of questions ends and the next begins.
Wide padding makes each button a bigger target that is easy to hit.
Wide padding keeps content clear of the strong border at any zoom.
Clear space between columns keeps values apart at high zoom.

open-ds.why: Big, even steps give an 8px base. Spacious density starts the tight gap at one and a half steps, so even close parts stay apart at high zoom.

We use 12px for the tight gap between the parts of one item in order to group and separate: one and a half base steps (1.5 × 8px), the smallest gap. Distance does this by grouping what is near and separating what is far, as the eye reads proximity (Gestalt), so a gap between groups stays clearly larger than a gap inside one. So parts read as one item and stay apart at high zoom, because steps are big and even (spacing.definition) and everyone uses it, including people with disabilities (people.q1).

We use 16px for the default gap between the items of one group, such as fields, in order to group and separate: two base steps (2 × 8px), 4px more than the tight gap. Distance does this by the rule given for space.gap.tight, so people with tremor tap the field they mean, because the layout is spacious (spacing.values) and space between fields matters most (spacing.lands).

We use 32px for the group gap between groups of questions in order to group and separate: four base steps (4 × 8px), twice the default gap. Distance does this by the rule given for space.gap.tight, so people see where one group of questions ends and the next begins, because the layout is spacious (spacing.values) and each step must take low effort to understand (human.q1).

We use 48px for the section gap between page sections in order to group and separate: six base steps (6 × 8px), half again the group gap. Distance does this by the rule given for space.gap.tight, so sections part by space, which is easy to see, and not by thin lines, because the layout is spacious (spacing.values) and steps are big and even (spacing.definition).

We use 24px for the inline padding inside controls in order to give content room inside its box: three base steps (3 × 8px), the same as a card's padding. Padding does this by keeping content off the edge of its box, so the content reads as part of that box, and by setting the size of the box with the content. So each button is a bigger target that is easy to hit, because everyone uses it, including people with motor needs (people.q1), and the smallest target is large (accessibility.values).

We use 24px for the padding inside cards and dialogs in order to give content room inside its box: three base steps (3 × 8px), half again the default gap. Padding does this by the rule given for space.inset.control-x, so content stays clear of the strong border at any zoom, because everyone uses it (people.q1) and each step must take low effort to understand (human.q1).

We use 16px for the inline padding inside table cells in order to give content room inside its box: two base steps (2 × 8px), the same as the default gap. Padding does this by the rule given for space.inset.control-x, so values in two columns stay apart at high zoom, because everyone uses it, including people with low vision (people.q1), and the layout is spacious (spacing.values).

We use 52px for one table row in order to keep the eye on its row: a row is one 52px default control tall, as rows stay one control tall. Row height does this by making each row a band the eye follows across, and a hit target when the row is clickable (WCAG 2.5.8: 24px). So rows are easy to read and tap, and a control sits in a row with no gap, because row heights are a spacing role, for touch and zoom (spacing.roles), and the smallest target is large (accessibility.values).
